Project 01 / Branding

Holistic Crunch

Brand identity

A brand identity built around the idea of a bite. I started from a hand-inked sketch of the lettering and rebuilt it as a vector wordmark with rough, crumbly edges, so the type looks like it was snapped off a bar.

The system has three lockups: the full wordmark, an HC monogram with crumbs flying off the C, and a stacked HO/CR mark with a bite taken out of the O.

What I focused onTurning a hand-drawn sketch into lettering that feels crunchy, in a warm brown and cream palette.
Project 02 / Logo design

Byte Talks

Speaker session logo

A logo for Byte Talks, a speaker session event at Google Developers Group. The heavy, stacked lettering reads like a stage billboard, and a grey 3D edge with a black outline lifts the white letters off the flat red.

Thin circuit traces and small square nodes run through the B, E, T and K, a quiet nod to the tech talks the sessions are about.

What I focused onBold type that is easy to read from the back of a hall, with one tech detail instead of many.
Project 03 / Poster design

Ghost

Cinematic poster

A poster inspired by the world of Ghost of Tsushima, blending Japanese aesthetics with a dark, dramatic style. I focused on typography, composition, imagery and atmosphere to capture Jin Sakai’s change from samurai to a warrior shaped by war.

What I focused onPink blossoms and red details are the only color in a grey ink-wash scene, so the eye lands on the title and the lone samurai.
ideas → pixels
Project 04 / Poster design

Democracy?

Protest poster

A socially driven poster created around the CJP protest. A huge condensed headline runs edge to edge, and the line “Too many voices to silence” is circled in loose, hand-drawn red-orange loops, like a pen mark on a printed page.

Press and protest photography is pushed into a two-tone orange and charcoal treatment, with a torn-paper photo frame, so the image reads fast and feels like a flyer. Two pull quotes balance the corners, one in English and one in Hindi written in Roman letters.

What I focused onBold typography, a strict colour limit and one strong image, so the urgency of the message comes through at a glance.
Project 05 / T-shirt design

Let me show you the future

Graphic tee

A T-shirt graphic for the line “Let me show you the future”, with my name set big underneath. Around the headline is a pile of early-computer nostalgia drawn in pixels: a cat peeking out of a loading window stuck at 69%, a retro calculator, a dino, a coffee mug, a cursor and clouds.

Cream and periwinkle on black keeps it to two light colours, so it prints cleanly on a dark tee and the headline still reads from a distance.

What I focused onMaking the headline the loudest thing, and letting the pixel icons add personality without crowding it.
Project 06 / UI & web design

Roots & Branches

Event landing page and registration

A landing page and registration portal for a Google Developers Group alumni event on 21-10-2026 in the CS-IT Seminar Hall. The line “Rooted in community. Growing beyond limits.” drives a glowing tree that grows through the whole page.

Visitors move from the event details to the speakers, previous events, a registration form and an FAQ.

What I focused onOne job per section, on a dark background, so people can find the date and sign up quickly.
Scroll inside the frame to see the full page.
Project 07 / UI/UX design

CropDoc

AI crop-health app for web and mobile

CropDoc helps farmers and gardeners spot leaf diseases early. People upload or photograph a leaf, the app analyses it with AI, and returns a result with a confidence score, a plain-language explanation and recommended next steps. The copy is careful to say these are likely matches, not a confirmed diagnosis.

I designed 36 screens for the full journey on web and mobile: the landing page, OTP verification, scanning and photo preview, the analysing state, scan results, history, a home screen with disease and gardening tips, and the error and empty states such as permission denied and no previous records. This page shows 7 of them.

What I focused onA calm green and cream palette, large readable type, and helpful states for waiting, errors and empty history, so people are never left guessing.
Project 08 / Social media design

How to make a bad UI design?

Educational carousel

A carousel that teaches good UI by showing what goes wrong. Each slide names a common mistake (inconsistent spacing, bad typography, too many colors, no space in your design) and pairs it with a short explanation and a small mock-up. The last slide turns the lessons into one rule: build a clear visual hierarchy so users know where to look first.

Drag or scroll sideways through the slides. Click to enlarge.
Project 09 / Video editing

Coming soon

“We will be back soon” teaser

A 16-second coming-soon teaser. It opens on a speaker in a Google Developers Group on Campus tee, holding a mic, cut in high-contrast black and white with diagonal wipes between shots.

The picture then drops to black, and the type glitches in with an RGB split before settling on “we will be back” and “soon”, with sound running underneath.

What I focused onShort, punchy cuts and one bold typeface, so a tiny teaser still builds anticipation.
